subject: Polity
description: Article 75, appointment, powers, removal, relation with President + Council

questions.stem: The Prime Minister of India is APPOINTED by the:

options.option_text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 75(1) — 'The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President.' Convention: President appoints the leader of the majority party / coalition in Lok Sabha as PM. If no clear majority — President exercises discretion (e.g., Sanjiva Reddy → Charan Singh, 1979). PM need not be MP at appointment but must become one within 6 months (Article 75(5)). Manmohan Singh was a Rajya Sabha member, never won LS election.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 75 of the Constitution says that the COUNCIL OF MINISTERS is collectively responsible to:

options.option_text: President of India and his cabinet

questions.explanation: Article 75(3) — 'Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the HOUSE OF THE PEOPLE.' Means: if LS passes a NO-CONFIDENCE motion, the WHOLE government must resign. Vajpayee govt fell by 1 vote in 1999 (269-270). PM personally responsible to LS. Note: Cabinet sails together, sinks together — collective responsibility is the cornerstone of parliamentary democracy. Rajya Sabha cannot remove government. Article 75(2) — 'Ministers hold office during the pleasure of President.'
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The MINIMUM AGE qualification to become Prime Minister of India is:
questions.explanation: PM must be a member of Parliament. Min age for: Lok Sabha = 25 years; Rajya Sabha = 30 years. So if PM is appointed via LS membership → 25; via RS → 30. Normally PM is from LS. Distractor 35 = President + Vice President min age. Note: Article 75(5) — non-MP can be appointed PM but must become MP within 6 months.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The PM is the head of the:
questions.explanation: PM = Head of GOVERNMENT (real executive). PRESIDENT = Head of STATE (nominal/ceremonial). PM chairs the Cabinet, allocates portfolios, removes ministers (advises Pres to). PM is the BRIDGE between President + Council, between government + Parliament, between government + the people. PM advises President on: appointments (Governors, AG, CAG, CEC, judges), dissolution of LS, summoning of sessions. India follows the BRITISH parliamentary model where PM = real chief executive.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The first PM to LOSE A NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION in Lok Sabha was:

options.option_text: Indira Gandhi after the Emergency time
Manmohan Singh on the nuclear deal

questions.explanation: MORARJI DESAI (Janata Party PM, 1977-79) — first to face + RESIGN before a no-confidence vote in July 1979 (knew he'd lose). Then Charan Singh became PM (only ~24 days, never faced LS — resigned). Vajpayee (1996, 13 days, resigned without facing vote; 1999 — actually LOST by 1 vote, government fell). The first PM whose government was DEFEATED in LS no-conf = VAJPAYEE 1999. The 1979 case was a resignation BEFORE vote. (Some texts treat Morarji as 'lost confidence', others as 'resigned without facing it'.)
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Article CAPS the size of the Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: Article 75(1A) — added by 91st AMENDMENT (2003): total Council of Ministers (including PM) shall not exceed 15% of total LS membership. With LS = 543, max ministers = 81. Rationale: prevent jumbo cabinets (Rajiv Gandhi had 60+ in 1989; UPA-1 had ~80). Same Amendment 91st added Article 75(1B) — defected MP cannot be made minister. Distractor 1: Article 74 says PM advises President (binding after 42nd Amend). Distractor 3: AG. Distractor 4: RS composition.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: On the resignation/death of the PM, the Council of Ministers automatically:

options.option_text: Continues with senior-most as acting PM

questions.explanation: Constitutional principle: PM is the keystone of the Council of Ministers. If PM resigns or dies → entire Council STANDS DISSOLVED automatically. President may ask the outgoing Council to continue as CARETAKER until a new government is formed. Examples: Nehru (died 1964) → Lal Bahadur Shastri became PM (Gulzarilal Nanda was acting PM for 13 days both times, in 1964 + 1966). After Indira (1984) → Rajiv. President swears in new PM, who then advises on Council. Distractor 1 partly true in practice via senior-most acting role, but Council itself dissolves.
